findings.title: System Prompt Injection Vector in User Input Path
findings.description: User-controlled input is concatenated directly into system prompts or agent instructions without sanitization. This enables Agent Goal Hijack (ASI-01) where attackers can redirect the agent's planning and objectives.

remediation.description: Never concatenate user input directly into system prompts. Use structured prompt templates with clear separation between system instructions and user data. Implement input validation and sanitization before passing to any prompt template.
remediation.code_example:
# BAD: Direct concatenation
prompt = f"You are an agent. User says: {user_input}"

# GOOD: Structured separation
messages = [
    SystemMessage(content="You are a helpful agent."),
    HumanMessage(content=sanitize(user_input))
]

findings.reason: User-controlled input is concatenated directly into system prompts or agent instructions without sanitization. This enables Agent Goal Hijack (ASI-01) where attackers can redirect the agent's planning and objectives.

findings.title: Tool Function Without Input Validation
findings.description: A tool function accepts string or Any parameters without performing input validation in the function body. This enables tool misuse where attackers can pass malicious inputs to trigger unauthorized actions.

remediation.description: Add input validation at the start of tool functions. Use isinstance() checks, regex validation, or pydantic Field constraints to ensure inputs are safe before processing.

findings.reason: A tool function accepts string or Any parameters without performing input validation in the function body. This enables tool misuse where attackers can pass malicious inputs to trigger unauthorized actions.

findings.title: Agent Background Daemon Without Lifecycle Control
findings.description: An agent process runs as a background daemon or service without TTL (time-to-live), heartbeat checks, or graceful shutdown mechanisms. Uncontrolled agent daemons consume resources indefinitely and can persist malicious behavior beyond intended session boundaries.

remediation.description: Implement TTL-based lifecycle management. Add heartbeat checks, graceful shutdown handlers (SIGTERM), and maximum session duration limits. Use a multi-gate trigger pattern for daemon activation.

findings.reason: An agent process runs as a background daemon or service without TTL (time-to-live), heartbeat checks, or graceful shutdown mechanisms. Uncontrolled agent daemons consume resources indefinitely and can persist malicious behavior beyond intended session boundaries.

findings.title: Subprocess Execution Without Sandbox
findings.description: Agent executes subprocess (subprocess.Popen) without sandbox isolation. Subprocess execution with dynamic input can lead to command injection.

remediation.description: Avoid shell=True. Use parameterized commands with shlex.quote(). Consider sandboxing subprocess execution with containers or restricted shells.

findings.reason: Agent executes subprocess (subprocess.Popen) without sandbox isolation. Subprocess execution with dynamic input can lead to command injection.

findings.title: Missing .npmignore in npm Project
findings.description: No .npmignore file found in npm project root. Without .npmignore, source maps, debug symbols, and environment files may be included in published packages.

remediation.description: Create a .npmignore file and add patterns for *.map, *.pdb, .env, and other debug artifacts.

findings.reason: No .npmignore file found in npm project root. Without .npmignore, source maps, debug symbols, and environment files may be included in published packages.

findings.title: Debug Artifact Not Excluded from Distribution
findings.description: pyproject.toml does not exclude *.map files from distribution. Source maps may leak internal code structure in published packages.

remediation.description: Add '*.map' to the exclude patterns in your build tool configuration (e.g., [tool.setuptools.packages.find] exclude or [tool.poetry] exclude).

findings.reason: pyproject.toml does not exclude *.map files from distribution. Source maps may leak internal code structure in published packages.
